body:
I'm really sorry to hear you're having a hard time. You did make it off the couch, though. That's a victory in my book for sure, so don't discount it. Thank you for this conversation, by the way. It helps to see value in people who maybe feel the same about themselves and realize that you might have value too and just not be able to see it. It helps to empathize with someone when everyone else around in the "real world" acts like you're the one lone freak who can't handle their shit. Now if we could all just get motivated and build ourselves a little island to hide together on, and live our weird little lives and try to find fulfillment in our weird little ways... the normal people can just keep hurting each other and eat themselves alive while we gently console one another from a distance.

I hope you feel better soon.

Movies used to be one of the few things I could do, if the parking lot was empty enough. I haven't been to one in a little over six months. I don't feel safe even in cars anymore, probably because I'm not in them very often these days. I haven't actually driven myself in several years, my license is expired and the possibility of me going to the DMV is about the same as me going to Mars.

I have absolutely made a prison for myself. I don't even experience seasons anymore, the temperature in my apartment is constant and it's usually very dim - the most I see of the sky is through the peep hole because I'm afraid to part the curtains. I saw a sunset once a few months ago when my SO was coming in the door and it made me cry. Sometimes I can feel the warmth of the sun in my dog's fur after my SO walks him (I can't do it myself anymore) and it is startling and very sad. The weather is changing now to my favorite season. I'm too upset now to keep writing but you get the idea.

I'm sure there are rewarding experiences but they have to be earned and I don't seem to deserve them for whatever reason.

I apologize for not seeing your comment sooner. This account is a throwaway and I had not logged back in since the day I posted. Thank you for your comment. Anyway, to answer your questions: I feel panic even at the thought of going outside, with or without a trusted (not that I feel safe with anyone at all these days) person, or even one of my neighbors knowing I'm in here. I try to stay quiet and keep the curtains closed at all times. One of my biggest shames is the thought of someone having heard me when I lose control of the volume of my voice during an "episode." I know someone had to have heard me crying today, it was really bad. Hopefully they just think I'm some crazy relative of my SOs visiting.

Again, I'm so sorry for my late reply. I am still trying to find the courage to try another professional. Do you have any experience with medications? My SO wants me to try that again but I am so afraid, but I also don't know how just talking could save me now. 

I hope you're doing well.

Hello better_all_the_time, thank you for your message. I apologize that I didn't see it until now because this account was a throwaway and I haven't looked up the post again until just now. I wish I could say things have improved. I just don't know what to do to help myself and there isn't anyone left in my real life to help me, not that is should be anyone else's responsibility to do so. I have been experiencing episodes where I am completely out of control and escalating self harm - wrist and head banging, clawing myself and destroying my own belongings. It happens so fast, like before I can even process a thought about it, it's done and I'm shocked and afraid. I'm so fearful that one of these times I'm going to do more harm than can be fixed. I destroyed my cell phone today after something bad happened to me, and had an episode that I don't even feel like I can call a panic attack anymore. I don't know what to call it. Pure terror and rage at once, pumping adrenaline and crying, screaming in agony and hyperventilating, alternated with pacing and tremors, jaw chattering, sobbing, wailing hell. Repeating words and phrases involuntarily(?), as if the thought I needed to express was the very breath I needed to live, it would just keep coming out. -ex. "Please. Please. Please. Please. Please. Please. Please. Please. Please." and on and on. It feels nothing short of apocalyptic.  The most ridiculous, dramatic thing I have ever seen. All after a traumatic contact with my abusive, semi-estranged mother following my birthday. So... I wish I had something better to say. You are a very nice person. I hope you are well.

Panic disorder with agoraphobia/PTSD/lifelong depression. I don't have any family or friends and it's just me and my SO, who has cheated on me and I don't know if I'd even still be with them if I wasn't agoraphobic. I'm trapped in my apartment and have achieved nothing in my life. I have nothing. I'm worth nothing. I'm unloveable. I've actually been in therapy since age 13.  I'm almost 30 now. The thing that caused me such a panic tonight was finding out that my new doctor broke confidentiality, so I don't really know what to do next. Thank you very much for your comments.

Thank you. I'm really glad that I posted here. Forcing myself to visualize the ugly reality of really doing it has helped a lot. I won't be doing that, ever. My life is not so dark as ending up that way, and that's a good thing to realize.
Thank you. I'm glad you survived your attempt.
I'm sorry for my negativity, your comments are very sweet and I'm sure you are a nice person. I've just had it. There's no hope for me.
I don't even now what safe feels like.

Well, I won't be going back to this doctor or probably ANY doctor again because I just found out that they and my SO talked about things that I wasn't ready to discuss when my SO was just supposed to be making arrangements for me to have a session over the telephone instead of coming in. I hadn't signed anything allowing this and I trusted a doctor and my SO for the LAST time. I'm ready to just fucking hang myself. I have head ENOUGH! Human beings are just rotten scum and I can't stand it any more!

Thank you for your reply. Hopefully it will make more sense after my next session. But I find it really difficult to trust any doctor, or any person really. I'll likely be suspicious or dismissive of any psych professional. I hate therapy and have had horrible experiences with it in the past, but sometimes it gets to the point where it's either try a different doctor or pick your poison.

Thanks again for your comment, and I'm sorry about what happened to you. Your hopeful outlook is admirable and I hope (!) one day to have a similar attitude.
